summary: Tightened the prose, replaced the unsupported 'European Parliament discussions' impact claim with the documented written question to the European Commission and named media coverage, corrected the CooRTweet developer description, restored the omitted doctorate, and moved the EACEA role to the past tense.

flags.claim: have informed discussions in the European Parliament
flags.issue: The authoritative biography supports only that the 2025 working paper was cited in a written question to the European Commission (European Parliament document E-10-2026-000086); 'informed discussions in the European Parliament' asserts a broader third-party effect than the source states. The uniurb.it press release claiming the study 'prompted a European Parliament inquiry' is a web mention and cannot support this. Replaced with the precise, supported claim.

The fact sheet states CooRTweet was developed by Nicola Righetti (Uniurb DISCUI) and Paul Balluff (GESIS); describing the developers as 'external teams' is inaccurate since Righetti is at Urbino. Corrected to name the developers.

flags.claim: guiding students and scholars through computational approaches to studying digital media ecosystem dynamics
flags.issue: Empty abstraction unsupported by any source and adding no information; removed in revision.

flags.claim: Fabio Giglietto is Full Professor of Internet Studies at the University of Urbino Carlo Bo
flags.issue: The authoritative biography also states he earned his doctorate at the same institution; the draft omitted this. Restored.

flags.claim: alongside performing expert proposal evaluations for the European Education and Culture Executive Agency
flags.issue: The EACEA appointment was stamped as running to September 2026; the draft's present-progressive phrasing implies ongoing currency the source does not assert beyond its stamp. Rephrased in the past tense as an appointment.

flags.claim: His recent empirical audits of platform algorithmic shifts and content reach restrictions
flags.issue: Vague plural ('audits') where the sources support one specific 2025 working paper on Meta's political content reduction policy; replaced with the specific, supported description.
